metadata.Description: An enhanced version of the French MEDIA Spoken Language Understanding (SLU) dataset. The original dataset, consisting of recorded phone calls for hotel booking, was only annotated for slots (concepts). This new version adds intent annotations using a semi-automatic tri-training methodology, enabling the development and evaluation of joint intent classification and slot-filling models.
metadata.Paper Title: New Semantic Task for the French Spoken Language Understanding MEDIA Benchmark
metadata.Venue Title: Proceedings of the Third Workshop on Deep Learning for Low-Resource Natural Language Processing
metadata.Venue Name: Third Workshop on Deep Learning for Low-Resource Natural Language Processing
metadata.Abstract: Intent classification and slot-filling are essential tasks of Spoken Language Understanding (SLU). In most SLU systems, those tasks are realized by independent modules. For about fifteen years, models achieving both of them jointly and exploiting their mutual enhancement have been proposed. A multilingual module using a joint model was envisioned to create a touristic dialogue system for a European project, HumanE-AI-Net . A combination of multiple datasets, including the MEDIA dataset, was suggested for training this joint model. The MEDIA SLU dataset is a French dataset distributed since 2005 by ELRA, mainly used by the French research community and free for academic research since 2020. Unfortunately, it is annotated only in slots but not intents. An enhanced version of MEDIA annotated with intents has been built to extend its use to more tasks and use cases. This paper presents the semi-automatic methodology used to obtain this enhanced version. In addition, we present the first results of SLU experiments on this enhanced dataset using joint models for intent classification and slot-filling.
